title: Is it weird to have the main player be stronger than the AI or is that normal?
author: No_Departure7494
selftext: My game is fair, but I die so much that half of the time is meant respawning and rejoining the battle. Do most games main the main character a bit stronger?

comments.author: jivenossauro
comments.body: Depends a lot on the game. Most games dont have the player in the same scale of power as the enemy, the most common from my experience is that the enemies have way more hp but way less damage than the player. What is your game about?

replies.author: No_Departure7494
replies.body: It's a combat game and the problem I keep facing is that when my tank is damaged I have to respawn and go back to the front. You can spawn closer, but not right in the action. I can't help but think to myself that maybe if the player was more survivable then this would be more enjoyable.

replies.author: jivenossauro
replies.body: It sounds like the player and the NPCs should be equal in your case. Maybe look into ways of reducing down time instead? Why not spawn right into action, or maybe add a revive mechanic?

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: In my car racing game, I've been striving to make the ai drivers better and better, til... oh shoot I can't outrun them. Sometimes the hard part of a game is making an enemy or opponent dumb enough. Treat it as a dial, if you've got it "too smart" and just dial it back til the balance of difficulty feels right, and see how other players fair at it.

comments.author: Motor-Travel-7560
comments.body:
There's a million different ways to give the player some sort of advantage to keep the game from feeling futile or cheap, and not even just by giving the player more HP or damage. 

For example, The old Castlevania games are hard AF in later levels because most enemies have more HP than you and do more damage. But the designers give you an advantage by opening each room in a way that you can watch the enemy patterns for as long as you want in order to figure out how to get around them.

comments.author: TimeAd7759
comments.body: go by the golden rule for game balance....Way more HP and way less damage on the bosses

comments.author: ItsDumi
comments.body: Most games are a power fantasy. So yes, the player is typically being setup to win with varying degrees of challenge. That depends on the player but even souls games are designed for the player to ultimately succeed

comments.author: erebusman
comments.body: Game balance is a tough topic in short : is the game fun for the target audience is what matters
